![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/37bf4ff4ad6eb63c9bf51bc5fd188ddc0f5bd58bfd4a097617f56fb5de151300.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by $y={x}^{3}$ and $y=x$ where $x\ge 0,$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{3}$ and $g(x)=x.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ {x}^{3} & =x \\ {x}^{3}-x & =0 \\ x({x}^{2}-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence $x=0$ and $x=\pm 1.$ But, since $x\ge 0,$ the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=1.$

Let's draw our vertical arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing *away* from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/f8850008be348bd78f48837def8691d3a4155e70d13909369c70da2eb31fffb4.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $y=f(x)={x}^{3},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $y=g(x)=x.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({[x]}^{2}-{[{x}^{3}]}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-{x}^{6})\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
